_readme: Round 8 (item 6): the checked-in allowlist of every declined_cases.json row whose on-device (device) or server (server) outcome knowingly differs from its true outcome (expect), or that is a pinned open defect (defect). Both table tests (app/test/engine/parser/declined_state_cues_table_test.dart, process-ios-sms/parse_test.ts) fail unless the set of deviating rows, with their device/server/defect values, equals this list and count. A completed row may deviate only to a more visible unrecorded outcome (device review / not_completed / transfer; server unresolved / not_completed / review = rejected with the device's own review row), never ignored, never another amount, never the opposite direction; 'dropped' (no amount read, a bank sender's Smart Inbox card) or another recorded type in the same direction is allowed (round 9). Round 10: Q's probes (V1-RES10) are added with their hand truth; an outcome the code still gets wrong on them (as at ab5dc10a or better) is pinned as an open defect (defect = 'OPEN ...'), and only those rows may carry one. Round 3 (closure): every row says what kind of pin it is: pin = 'safe_deviation' (a characterization: a side knowingly differs from the true outcome in the safe direction, never a total change) or 'open_defect' (a characterization of a known wrong outcome, with defect). A table row that is not in this list is an acceptance row: both sides must reach its expect. When a fix makes a side reach expect, its pin is removed (moved to acceptance). The list may not grow without editing the ceiling (maxCount) in both table tests. Round 5 (owner decision, completion certainty): a completed row that is not clearly completed (a doubt word anywhere outside security advice, or no completed-event form) is kept for review on both sides - device = review, server = unresolved - a safe deviation by the owner rule (counted in the round-5 acceptance as an unnecessary review).
